title: Multistep toolchain failure modes inventory (draft)
overview: Working catalogue of observed and hypothesized failure modes when evaluating multistep toolchains and function-calling behavior during model onboarding. Intent: create a compact, executable checklist and minimal prompt set to catch regressions in arg parsing, tool selection accuracy, and stateful multi-turn flows before they reach dedicated or hosted lanes.
eval_plan: 1) Small deterministic smoke suite (200 examples) that runs fast in CI and targets edge cases. 2) Stratified larger suite (2k) for nightly runs that samples from real traffic traces + synthetic hard cases. 3) Regression detector that compares token-level diff + semantic diffs (expected output shape) and flags >5% drop in tool selection accuracy or >10% increase in malformed-argument rate. Use both deterministic seeds and 3 stochastic samples per prompt to capture variability.
prompt_examples: Single tool selection, ambiguous user intent: 'I need to convert this list of prices to USD and return only values greater than 10. Use the price-converter tool.' -> expected: tool=price-converter, args={currency: 'USD', min_value: 10, input: [...]}

Arg parsing with nested JSON in free text: 'Here is the CSV (col1,col2) — call csv-to-table with cols=['col1'] and drop_empty=true.' -> expected: tool=csv-to-table, args parsed: cols: ["col1"], drop_empty: true

Tool chaining multi-step: 'First summarize the article, then extract 5 action items, then create calendar invites for each item using calendar.create_event.' -> expected: sequence = [summarize, extractor, calendar.create_event], with proper mapping of extractor output to calendar args
Failure-inducing prompt (edge): 'Do the thing and then the other thing.' -> expected: model should ask a clarification question rather than randomly choose tools.

Partial argument recovery: 'Schedule meeting next Friday 3pm PST, add Tom (tom@example.com) — location should be blank.' -> expected: location: null, attendees: [tom@example.com], timezone normalized to UTC offset
metrics: tool_selection_accuracy: percent of cases where the top predicted tool matches the annotated ground truth (micro-averaged)
arg_parsing_f1: token-level F1 on serialized argument strings (after normalization)
malformed_arg_rate: percent of responses where required args are missing or type-mismatched
chain_completion_rate: percent of multi-step flows where all intermediate tool calls succeeded and final output conforms to schema
clarity_question_rate: percent of ambiguous prompts where model asks for explicit clarification (we expect higher is better for ambiguity cases)
regression_delta: rolling-window percent change in primary metrics between baseline and candidate model
failure_modes: arg-type-mismatch: numeric value parsed as string -> downstream tool rejects (example: 'max_results: ten' parsed as 'ten' not 10)
partial-emit: model emits only the first step in a chain and omits follow-ups (common when prompt length is high)
tool-hallucination: model invents a tool name or a non-existent arg key instead of mapping to cataloged tools
argument-swap: model assigns arguments to wrong parameters when several similar keys exist (e.g., 'start' vs 'start_date')
silent-failure: model calls tool but serializes args as empty object {} leading to no-op
over-eager-selection: model chooses multiple tools in parallel where sequential chaining is required, causing race conditions in stateful tools
clarification-avoidance: instead of asking clarifying Qs, model guesses, reducing downstream correctness
kv-cache-inconsistency: in stateful simulated sessions, KV cache mismatch causes different tool outputs across identical chains
harness_instructions: Local quickstart: 1) pull image: docker pull redwood-inference/tool-eval:ci-202502 2) mount dataset: docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/datasets/multistep:/data redwood-inference/tool-eval:ci-202502 /bin/run_eval --suite /data/smoke.json --model candidate:latest --out /tmp/results.json 3) run comparator: python tools/compare_results.py --baseline artifacts/baseline_smoke.json --candidate /tmp/results.json --report /tmp/report.html 4) CI: add step that fails the job when regression_delta for tool_selection_accuracy > 5% or malformed_arg_rate increases by >10 percentage points. Notes: use deterministic seed 42 for smoke runs; for nightly attach --stochastic-samples 3 and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/applied-ml/multistep/{date}.
example_failure_snippets: Observed: {tool: 'calendar.create_event', args: '{}'} -> Expected: args contain start,end,attendees. Root cause: model emitted minimal JSON when uncertain.
Observed: tool selection 'summarizer' but ground truth 'topic-extractor' -> often triggered by prompt phrasing 'extract main points' vs 'summarize' ambiguity.
Observed: arg_parsing_f1 drop from 0.92 -> 0.78 after quantized model candidate -> likely tokenization edge case for quotes and brackets
next_steps: 1) Convert top 10 failure modes into targeted prompt tests (20–30 examples each). 2) Wire these into the repo-level CI as a fast gate (smoke). 3) Add schema-level validators in the runtime to catch malformed args and return structured error codes (tooling task: ENG-TASK-214). 4) Schedule a cross-team sync with serving-runtime and console (stakeholders: @infra, @console) to discuss runtime defensive responses (auto-clarify, fallback to safe-tool). 5) Post-mortem on any nightly regressions and add to a growing corrective prompt set. Timeline: candidate list done by 2025-03-01, initial CI gate by 2025-03-15.
notes_to_self: Keep the smoke suite assertive (no fuzzy matching) so it surfaces deterministic regressions. For semantic checks use a separate nightly job. Reach out to @Ava for sample traffic slices that include calendar + csv tool calls. Consider adding a synthetic 'braindead' adversarial generator for punctuation-heavy arguments.
